title: Binary Tree: Level-order Traversal (BFS)
summary: Visit a binary search tree level by level with a queue: take a node from the front, visit it, then add its children to the back.

inputs.name: values
inputs.label: Values to insert (in order)
inputs.note: They are inserted into a binary search tree first: smaller values go left, others go right.

anchors.label: Put the root in the queue
While the queue is not empty

practice.note: The tree arrives as `root` (None or null when empty), built by inserting the values one at a time into a binary search tree (smaller goes left, equal or larger goes right). A TreeNode has `val`, `left` and `right`. Return the values level by level, left to right, as a list.
